text: FOR ANYONE WHO READS THIS: If you have problems with this particular card not accepting the Radeon driver, it's because it's been factory bios-modded and AMD cut off modded bios support on 4xx cards, but not 5xx cards. You CAN get around this by using ToastyX's AMD ATI Pixel Clock Patcher patching only the bios check. Also if you find one be careful as fan is not perfect and while noisy and still less than reference 480, it won't be capable of cooling at more than 1350mhz turbo speed +0mV in intensive scenarios, this is why the 5xx came out and no other reason, it just simply runs cooler delta to be able to run @ 1400.

You could always just use MSI afterburner and set a custom fan profile. You could even have the fans not turn on until it gets really hot (or at least really low) if you want it to run quite.

Other thing, are you running multiple monitors? My R9 270 would engage gaming mode (10x memory speed and 4x (I think) GPU speed) when I hooked up 2 monitors. The temps would go way up though just due to frequency (though manually you could under-clock it and it was fine), but you don't have high temps, so I'm not really sure. text: Why isn't there more games? I love this channel, but this looks like they've taken only those games, that were able to get 60+ fps. I've checked benchmarks made by polish site, and FPS for GTA V on maximum settings in Vinewood are 42 at average with dips below 35. Witcher 3 on max settings (without hairworks ofc) is on 50 avg. with dips to 44 and  even Rise of the Tomb Rider, which is shown in this video, on very high with FXAA achieves average of 50 FPS. For me 1080p sweetspot is a card, that will run any current game on max settings in 1080p with 60 fps (ofc with disabled those "extra" settings that literally kill framerate, like hairworks in W3 or advanced physX in other games) and also that will be able to run like this (maybe just a bit slower) all new games that will come out in 1,5-2 years. But maybe it's just me. Now for more than 4 years I've been running a 670 and I don't regret a single penny I've spent on it. Sure, cheaper cards gives better bang for buck, but my card did excactly what I wrote: ran all new games for 2 years at max settings in 1080p, and even now I run W3 at almost highest settings, and get above those 35 FPS. And with some compromises I get solid 60FPS, but I'm type of person that prefers visuals over fps to some degree. If I bought RX470 now, I'd be worried that after 2 years I won't be able to run some new games with satysfying visuals and framerate, which would lead me to buy a new card. So are cheaper cards really cheaper? Is RX470 going to hold on for 4 years? I don't know :D BTW, I just realised that I wrote a whole essay up there XD

text:
okay, so let me get things straight.

Both cards are not meant to be compared in any way.

The 1060 is a 1440p@60hz or 1080p144hz (in some games like CS:GO and older ones) card.
The 470 is a pure 1080p@60hz card. It reaches those frames in any game (as shown in this video)

Now, if you don't plan on using 144hz (which is a bless in some games, but also requires an adequate GPU) any time soon, save some money and go for the 470, as you can't differentiate between lets saay 60 and 100fps. As long as you don't run a monitor with a higher refresh rate of course.

That almost 100$ can be spent on a better SSD, CPU, case, an AIO liquid cooler and many many other things that would make you happier than reaching more than 60 fps on a monitor with 60hz. Period.

If you plan on buying a 1440p or 144hz 1080p monitor, like me get the 1060. (I will wait for the 490 and either get that or the 1070, depending on price/performance ofc and then get either a 1440p or 144hz 1080p monitor later down the line, as I can't afford both at the same time)


!BUT! you could also see the 1060 get beaten by the 470 in Vulkan. Now why should that be of any concern to you? 

That's simple. Because that's what will be replacing DX11 (along with DX12 and OpenGL of course).
I personally don't plan on changing my GPU every generation (which is the mentality of most consumers), but look a bit into the future for every GPU I purchase.

Vulkan was basically built with AMD GPUs in mind, therefore pretty much always performing better for team red.

Similar story with DX12. Let's say both companies are identical in software support for that... AMD still has the edge because of superior hardware (asynchronous compute units or ACU for short). These also make it VERY unlikely for NVidia ever having the chance of beating AMD in terms of percentage performance increase over DX11.

While the 1060 may beat the 470 still by a small margin on paper, that will never be as grave so you could see it.


Broken down: 1060 for 1440p@60hz or 1080p@144hz (some games).
470 for 1080p@60hz (spend your money on other parts that will have more impact than 40fps you can't even see, because of monitor limitations).
